In src/sqllens/tools/_format.py, _table_block_to_markdown (about lines 1159-1198) builds the display-cut note. It reads kept = row_count (N), dropped = truncated (K) and total = kept + dropped (M). When dropped > 0 it sets shown = min(kept, 500), which is R = min(N,500). It then emits 'Showing the first {shown} of {total} rows. The other {dropped} rows were left out to fit the display size limit.', which states R, M and K. When shown < kept (R<N) it appends 'This Markdown table lists at most 500 rows.' The old 'Showing first 500 of N rows.' footer is now an elif branch that runs only when dropped == 0, so the new note replaces it for display-cut tables. The note is appended to the same Markdown string as the table, so it is part of the table's Markdown. It holds at M<=500 because shown = kept and no 'at most' sentence is added. It holds at R<500<M because shown = kept < 500 and total > 500. I read the source only and ran no tests, so I did not check the tests.
